## Summary

Under Section 165(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, a person may hold office as a director, including as an alternate director, in **up to 20 companies at the same time**.

The maximum number of **public companies** in which the person may be appointed as a director is **10**. Directorships in private companies that are holding or subsidiary companies of public companies are included when calculating the public-company limit. Directorship in a dormant company is excluded from the overall limit of 20.

A company’s members may, by special resolution, prescribe a lower limit for its director.

Legal currentness is unverified. This is legal information, not legal advice.

## Relevant quotation

“No person ... shall hold office as a director, including any alternate directorship, in more than twenty companies at the same time.”

“The maximum number of public companies in which a person can be appointed as a director shall not exceed ten.”

The supplied evidence defines a private company as one whose articles, except in the case of a One Person Company, limit its members to **two hundred**. However, the evidence provided does not expressly state the minimum incorporation requirement of two persons.

- Capable of distinguishing the goods or services of one person from those of others.

It may include the **shape of goods, their packaging, or a combination of colours**.
